label: digit 0 input at original positions 0-2
explanation: Fires only when the input token is the digit 0 during the original (pre-<DEL>) phase at one of the first three positions (t = 0, 1, 2). It never fires on any other token, on <DEL>, or in the copy phase, including when 0 is fed back as a copied output. Magnitude falls off with position: t = 0 is near max (~1.8), t = 1 is around 0.8-0.9 of max, t = 2 is around 0.3-0.6. Activation mass shares are 46% / 35% / 19% over similar step counts. At t = 3 it fires only weakly and rarely (about 4% of all steps, 0.3% of mass); from t >= 4 it never fires. A 0 that repeats an earlier 0 fires more weakly. Dev split: precision 1.0, recall 0.96, mass recall 0.997.

issues: I reproduced the test scores exactly: precision 1.0, recall 0.962, F1 0.980, mass recall 0.997. There were 0 false positives on the test split.

The profile confirms the claim that it never fires in the delimiter or copy phase (0 active steps in both), never fires for t >= 4, and fires only on in_tok == 0. The mass shares by t are 0.462, 0.348 and 0.187, as stated.

The only misses are 2019 steps at t = 3 holding 0.3% of the mass, as the explanation says. Firing at t = 3 is rare and weak: adding t == 3 to the predicate has precision 0.12, and widening to t <= 3 drops F1 to 0.88. So excluding t = 3 is the right choice.
The claim that a repeated 0 fires more weakly was not scored, but the explanation already says so. It is a minor point either way.
